subject: Dark-site image rotation and authority handoff — prep and schedule
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: ACME CloudOps <ops@acmecloud.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dark-site image rotation and authority handoff — prep and schedule

Hi team,

We have a scheduled dark-site (air-gapped) image rotation for Kite Financial's isolated cluster the week of May 17. This thread is to align the technical handoff and the courier/operator ceremony. Key points we need confirmed before the window: 

- Signed artifact: attached signed-manifest-v1.json (SHA256 checksums + signature). Will you be able to validate signature chain on arrival?
- Key transport: we will ship an HSM-wrapped operator token and a sealed operator envelope. Confirm who will perform the unwrap (on-site operator vs SecureTrans custodian).
- NTP drift window: plan for a 30s tolerance; offline env will not have NTP. We will use a time-anchor token in the manifest.
- Console fallback: please confirm serial/OOB console access so we can run the validation script if networked verification fails.
- Acceptance paperwork: operator must sign the acknowledgement (DocuSign link to follow).

Tentative schedule:
- May 17 09:00 local: courier arrival and manifest handoff
- May 17 10:00 local: operator unwrap and signature verification
- May 17 11:00-13:00 local: install and smoke tests

Action: Can ACME Ops confirm courier ETA and on-site operator identity by EOD May 4?

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Trust & Security
Redwood Inference
Attachment: signed-manifest-v1.json (application/json, 14 KB)

From: ACME CloudOps <ops@acmecloud.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dark-site image rotation and authority handoff — prep and schedule

Evelyn / team,

Thanks for the heads-up and the manifest. Quick answers and a few clarifying questions (we reproduced the header you sent):

> - Signed artifact: attached signed-manifest-v1.json (SHA256 checksums + signature). Will you be able to validate signature chain on arrival?

We can validate the chain on-site using our offline verification station. Please confirm the root certificate thumbprint and whether the chain uses an intermediate signing key bound to the depot ID. Our verification script expects: SHA256, PKCS7 detached signature, and a PEM bundle for the chain.

> - Key transport: we will ship an HSM-wrapped operator token and a sealed operator envelope. Confirm who will perform the unwrap (on-site operator vs SecureTrans custodian).

SecureTrans will only courier the parcel to the site and provide identity verification upon delivery. The unwrap must be done by the on-site operator or an appointed agent from Kite Financial. Courier will witness chain-of-custody only.

Questions:
- Can Redwood provide the HSM wrapping metadata (KMS key id / KDF parameters) and the operator public key so we can pre-populate validation tooling?
- Is there an emergency fallback image if verification fails?

We will confirm ETA and operator identity by EOD May 6.

Regards,
Ravi Patel
Lead Cloud Operations
ACME CloudOps
Attachment: none

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: ACME CloudOps <ops@acmecloud.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dark-site image rotation and authority handoff — prep and schedule

Thanks Ravi — answers below and an attached checklist. I've also included a couple of low-level validation commands so your offline station can run a deterministic check once the bundle arrives.

Summary answers: 
- Root cert thumbprint: SHA256: 3f:9a:...:b8 (full fingerprint provided in the Drive link below). We do use an intermediate signing key that is rotated per-release; the signed-manifest includes the intermediate cert.
- Signature format: PKCS7 detached with SHA256. We include a PEM bundle in signed-manifest-v1.json under the signatures block.
- HSM wrapping metadata: KMS id: rwd-kms-prod-07, wrapping algorithm: RSA-OAEP-256, KDF: HKDF-SHA256. We'll deliver the wrapping metadata file alongside the manifest.
- Emergency fallback: yes — there is a minimal rollback image (rollback-v3.tar.gz) signed by the root. If verification fails we will default to rollback-v3 (operator must acknowledge).

Verification commands (offline station):
- Extract checksum: jq -r '.checksums["image.bin"]' signed-manifest-v1.json | xxd -r -p | sha256sum
- Verify PKCS7: openssl cms -verify -inform PEM -in signature.p7s -content image.bin -CAfile chain.pem -out /dev/null

Operator unwrap model: the on-site operator will unwrap. SecureTrans will not perform unwrap. The on-site operator must present two forms of identity per the acknowledgement doc.

I attached a short offline-manifest-checklist.pdf that enumerates the acceptance steps (verify hash, verify signature, check timestamps, run self-check). Note: because the target cluster is isolated we recommend the following tolerance for the time-anchor: +/- 45 seconds. The agent that runs the verification will write the operator-handback.json into the escrow folder and the courier will include MD5 manifest for transit proof.

Let me know if you want a dry run with the verification station prior to shipment — we can schedule a remote test using a sealed test bundle.

Jonas Weber
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: offline-manifest-checklist.pdf (application/pdf, 52 KB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: ACME CloudOps <ops@acmecloud.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Thanks,
Evelyn

Redwood Inference
